introText: ECRS is a nonprofit organization founded in 1940 to provide cooperative recreation as a way to rest and refresh, to add richness and depth to living, and to aid the development of communities and humanity at large. For more than 85 years it has rested on the belief that recreation is the way to richer lives, and an important tool for teachers, social workers, and anyone else who works with people, whether as a volunteer or for pay. The crazy experiment started in the '40s is working.

nameParts.text: The group was centered in the eastern part of the United States. When ECRS began, the idea was that there would be cooperative recreation schools in other regions too, and ECRS became one of several dozen regional recreation workshops, or "rec labs," across North America. Our region runs up and down the eastern seaboard, mainly from Maine to Virginia, with members in Canada and well beyond.
ECRS is run by its members, who work together for the good of everyone. Everyone chips in to help with jobs at events, like providing late-night snacks or decorating for New Year's Eve.
The founding tenet was that play is an integral part of life for adults and children alike, and that it is necessary for mental health and well-being.

ECRS emphasizes learning and leadership. It has served as a training ground for many professionals and volunteers in recreation leadership, with mentors who support, encourage, and help guide each new leader.

timeline.text: ECRS is founded. Its early decades are told in the words of the people who lived them in [Of Play and Playfulness](/of-play-and-playfulness/past-present-future).
ECRS publishes [Of Play and Playfulness](/of-play-and-playfulness), a collection of recreational activities, memories, and reflections from its first fifty years.

ECRS celebrates 60 years with an anniversary weekend at the Hemlocks Conference Center in Hebron, Connecticut. The year's calendar includes a Spring Weekend at Stony Point, two camping weekends at Camp Onas, Summer School and Winter Workshop at Watson Homestead, and fun days in town.
Summer School moves to Powell House, a Quaker retreat center in Old Chatham, New York.
The 70th Anniversary Winter Workshop at Watson Homestead.
About 100 people of all ages celebrate 75 years at Camp Harlam in the Poconos. Winter Workshop becomes Winter Adventure.
During the pandemic, ECRS moves online with virtual weekends, ice cream socials, and Winter Connections, then returns to in-person events.

evolvingText: Classes at ECRS events have expanded beyond the traditional core of games, informal dramatics, and song. Newer experiences include self-exploration (Making the Change You Want; Taking Stock and Moving Forward), live-action role playing (Adventure Games), and forays into drumming and puppetry. Browse [past events](/events) to see how the program has grown.
